idStrategy.legacyId: Older source ID or internal ID retained for traceability when the human-facing code changed.
idStrategy.displayId: Human-facing criterion code from the revised SD Standard document.
idStrategy.subcategory: Slug-style subcategory used for grouping, filtering, and docs generation.
idStrategy.appliesTo: Applicability marker from the revised SD Standard document: project, designingEntity, or both.

ethical-practices-in-design-and-producti.label: Ethical Practices in Design and Production

economic-accountability-and-strategic-va.label: Economic Accountability and Strategic Value / Financial Planning

criteria.label: Environmental Impact Reduction
criteria.description: The project strategy includes at least one action to reduce environmental impact that is supported by a qualified life cycle study (LCS) or quantitative life cycle assessment (LCA).
criteria.whyItMatters: Actions lead to designs with a lower impact.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to all projects.

criteria.summary: Reduces environmental impact and is supported by a qualified life cycle study (LCS) or quantitative life cycle assessment (LCA).

criteria.label: Product Ingredients Transparency
criteria.description: The project includes a list of all components and/or ingredients.
criteria.whyItMatters: The display of “ingredients” or material components.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is mainly relevant to packaging or products with material disclosure needs.

criteria.summary: Displays ingredients or material components.

criteria.label: Ink, Printing, and Finishes
criteria.description: The project reduces or eliminates the use of inks, varnishes and finishes, or requires no printing.
criteria.whyItMatters: Reduces ink coverage on printed materials.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is typically not relevant for screen-only outputs.

criteria.summary: Reduces ink coverage on printed materials.

criteria.label: Paper
criteria.description: The project reduces paper use through efficiencies.
criteria.whyItMatters: Efficient use of paper and reduces paper use.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion generally does not apply to purely digital projects.

criteria.summary: Reduces paper use.

criteria.label: Product Quantity
criteria.description: Reproduction is limited to immediate needs, including the possibility that no physical copies were needed.
criteria.whyItMatters: Reproduction and end-of-life considerations.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies where physical production volume is relevant.

criteria.summary: Considers reproduction needs.

criteria.label: Durability & Extended Life
criteria.description: The product or system is physically durable and has a longer life than the industry average, where desirable. The product or system can be reused, recharged, repaired, and/or upgraded as an environmental benefit.
criteria.whyItMatters: Product design for longer life than the industry average.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is most relevant where a product, system, or durable output can remain in use over time.

criteria.summary: Integrates extended-life durability through reuse, repair, recharge, and/or upgrade where appropriate.

criteria.label: Toxins
criteria.description: The project reduces or eliminates the use of toxins.
criteria.whyItMatters: Reduces or eliminates toxins in a product.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies primarily when physical materials are selected.

criteria.summary: Reduces or eliminates toxins.

criteria.label: Environmental Policy
criteria.description: The design entity and a majority of suppliers have publicly-accessible environmental policies.
criteria.whyItMatters: Publicly-accessible environmental policies.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to most projects.

criteria.summary: Displays publicly-accessible environmental policies.

criteria.label: Animal Welfare
criteria.description: To the best of the design entity's knowledge, the project, the design entity, and the client's activities do not, and will not, put animals at risk.
criteria.whyItMatters: Animals are not at risk from this project.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when the project affects ecosystems, sourcing, or wildlife-related outcomes.

criteria.summary: Protects all animals.

criteria.label: Ecosystems Conservation
criteria.description: To the best of the design entity's knowledge, the project, the design entity, and the client's activities do not, and will not, support the destruction of ecosystems.
criteria.whyItMatters: Conservation of valuable ecosystems.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when the project affects ecosystems, sourcing, or wildlife-related outcomes.

criteria.summary: Conserves valuable ecosystems.

criteria.label: Recyclability or Reusability
criteria.description: Materials or systems used increase the ease and likelihood of recycling and/or reuse of the product and its packaging.
criteria.whyItMatters: Product and packaging can be reused or recycled.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies mainly to physical products and materials.

criteria.summary: Enables recycling or reuse.

criteria.label: Non-Renewable Resources
criteria.description: The project reduces or eliminates the use of scarce, non-renewable natural resources and raw materials.
criteria.whyItMatters: Strategies reduce the use of non-renewable natural resources.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion mainly applies to material-based projects.

criteria.summary: Reduces non-renewable natural resources and materials.

criteria.label: Biological or Organic Materials
criteria.description: The product can be used as fuel or food, or composted, either locally composted by the end user or incorporated into a local energy-recovery system that does not involve landfill or thermal treatment.
criteria.whyItMatters: The product can be composted or used as fuel or food.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion mainly applies to physical outputs with material end-of-life considerations.

criteria.summary: Uses waste as a nutrient or fuel, or is compostable.

criteria.label: Zero Waste
criteria.description: The final product is a "zero waste" product.
criteria.whyItMatters: Zero waste products.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion mainly applies to physical products or installations.

criteria.summary: Eliminates waste.

criteria.label: Renewable Energy
criteria.description:
Project: The production of the product uses renewable energy from solar, wind, thermal or tidal sources.

Design Entity: The design entity uses renewable energy from solar, wind, thermal or tidal sources.
criteria.whyItMatters: Clean energy sources were used to make the product.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion may apply to printers, hosts, platforms, venues, and other suppliers.

criteria.summary: Uses renewable energy.

criteria.label: Consumer Energy Efficiency
criteria.description: The product or system used by the consumer is energy efficient or uses renewable energy.
criteria.whyItMatters: The product consumes energy efficiently.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when the end-user experience consumes electricity or device resources.

criteria.notes: Source document includes a note to add an energy efficiency criterion, perhaps including energy use of AI.
criteria.summary: Optimizes consumer energy efficiency.

criteria.label: Energy Efficiency
criteria.summary: Maximizes the product or the system's energy efficiency.
criteria.description: The product or system used by the consumer is energy efficient or uses renewable energy.

criteria.label: Storage and Transportation
criteria.description: The project includes shipping and/or warehousing efficiencies to optimize storage and transportation.
criteria.whyItMatters: Efficiency in the product’s transportation.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when physical distribution or warehousing is part of the project.

criteria.summary: Optimizes storage and transportation efficiencies.

criteria.label: Quantified GHG Reporting and Certification
criteria.description:
Project: The project has a publicly-accessible quantified report of GHG reductions and/or energy, material use and waste disposal.

Design Entity: The design entity has a publicly-accessible quantified report of GHG reductions and/or energy, material use and waste disposal.
criteria.whyItMatters: Publicly-accessible reporting of materials, waste and emissions.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant at the organizational level.

criteria.summary: Displays a publicly-accessible report of emissions, materials use, and waste.
criteria.resourcesNote: These tools provide indicative website-impact estimates. They do not provide formal GHG certification or verified carbon accounting and should not be presented as evidence of either.

resources.title: EcoGrader
resources.description: A website sustainability assessment tool that estimates digital carbon emissions and evaluates factors such as page weight, performance, hosting, and user experience. Useful for establishing a baseline, identifying opportunities to reduce a website’s digital footprint, and tracking improvements over time.

resources.title: Website Carbon Calculator
resources.description: A simple tool for estimating the carbon emissions associated with loading a web page. Useful as an accessible first-pass estimate of the environmental impact of websites and for comparing design or development alternatives.

criteria.label: Air Pollution
criteria.description:
Project: The project reduces or avoids air pollution.

Design Entity: The design entity reduces or avoids air pollution.
criteria.whyItMatters: Product emission and air pollution.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion can apply across many project types.

criteria.summary: Reduces air pollution.

criteria.label: Carbon Offsets
criteria.description:
Project: The project offsets all GHG emissions for travel, production and Web presence.

Design Entity: The design entity offsets all GHG emissions for travel, production and Web presence.
criteria.whyItMatters: Carbon credits offset travel, production and Web presence.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when offsetting is part of the strategy.

criteria.summary: Offsets travel, production, and web presence emissions through carbon credit purchases.

criteria.label: Water
criteria.description: Water pollution or water use were avoided or reduced.
criteria.whyItMatters: Reduces water use and pollution.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion mainly applies where materials or production processes use water.

criteria.summary: Reduces or eliminates water use and water pollution.

criteria.label: Sound & Light Pollution
criteria.summary: Reduces or eliminates sound and light pollution.
criteria.description:
Project: The project avoids or reduces sound and light pollution.

Design Entity: The design entity avoids or reduces sound and light pollution.

criteria.label: Odor, Scent and Fragrance
criteria.summary: Eliminates odors, scents and fragrances.
criteria.description:
Project: The project is odor, scent, and fragrance-free.

Design Entity: The design entity has a no odor, scent, or fragrance policy.

criteria.label: Harmless
criteria.description: The project reduces mental and physical injury to those who produce or use the product.
criteria.whyItMatters: Reduces injury in the making and use of the product.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to all projects.

criteria.summary: Reduces injury in the making and use of the product.

criteria.label: Health and Safety
criteria.description: The project improves the health or safety of the target audience.
criteria.whyItMatters: Improves human health and/or safety.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is most relevant when health or safety outcomes are central to the project brief.

criteria.summary: Improves human health and/or safety.

criteria.label: Local Labour
criteria.description: The project significantly increases the amount of locally sourced labour from the end users' location.
criteria.whyItMatters: Increases locally sourced labour.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion can apply across project types when labour sourcing is a strategic choice.

criteria.summary: Increases locally sourced labour.

criteria.label: Human Rights
criteria.description:
Project: To the best of the design entity's knowledge, the project and the client's activities are not directly or indirectly involved in the violation of universal human rights.

Design Entity: The design entity does not contribute directly or indirectly to the violation of universal human rights.
criteria.whyItMatters: Design does not contribute to the violation of human rights.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to all projects.

criteria.summary: Upholds universal human rights.
criteria.category: Ethical Practices in Design and Production

criteria.label: Corruption
criteria.description:
Project: To the best of the design entity's knowledge, the project and the client's activities are not directly or indirectly involved in corruption or unethical governance.

Design Entity: The design entity is not involved in corruption or unethical governance.
criteria.whyItMatters: Corruption was not identified in the project.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to all projects.

criteria.summary: Upholds high standards of anti-corruption and ethical governance.
criteria.category: Ethical Practices in Design and Production

criteria.label: Rights of Workers
criteria.description: To the best of the design entity's knowledge, the project and the client's activities are not directly or indirectly involved in the violation of the fundamental principles and rights of workers.
criteria.whyItMatters: Upholds the rights of workers.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to all projects.

criteria.summary: Upholds the rights of workers.
criteria.category: Ethical Practices in Design and Production

criteria.label: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
criteria.description: The project discloses the sources of design whether human made or AI generated. If AI was used to create any part of a design, it follows UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence.
criteria.whyItMatters: Authentically created design by a person.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to all projects.

criteria.summary: Discloses design sources as human-made or AI generated, and adheres to ethical guidelines.
criteria.category: Ethical Practices in Design and Production

criteria.label: Electronic Documents
criteria.description: All electronic documents comply with the W3C WCAG 2.0 Level A standard, or higher, or comply with the ISO standard for PDF/UA accessibility standard.
criteria.whyItMatters: Accessibility of all electronic documents, including Web pages.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies to digital or hybrid outputs with electronic documents or interfaces.

criteria.summary: Ensures accessibility of all electronic documents, including Web pages.

criteria.label: Printed Documents and Compliance
criteria.description: Printed materials are designed using accessible typography, contrast, hierarchy, and readability principles to support users with visual, cognitive, or literacy-related accessibility needs.
criteria.whyItMatters: Accessibility of printed documents.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies to digital or hybrid documents and content systems.

criteria.summary: Ensures accessibility of all printed materials.

criteria.label: Universal Design Principles
criteria.description: The non-document components of the project adhere to universal design principles.
criteria.whyItMatters: Complies with Universal Design standards.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant across physical and digital experiences.

criteria.summary: Complies with Universal Design standards.

criteria.label: Intellectual Property
criteria.description: The project clearly defines and respects intellectual property ownership, authorship, permissions, licensing, and usage rights. Where appropriate, the project may also share reusable intellectual property through Creative Commons or another open licensing approach that creates value for society.
criteria.whyItMatters: Clear intellectual property ownership, permissions, licensing, and usage rights protect creators, users, clients, and the public value of reusable design work.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when reuse, open licensing, or public benefit knowledge-sharing are part of the project.

criteria.summary: Uses a clear and responsible intellectual property approach.

criteria.label: Affordable
criteria.description: The product is affordable to a wide audience including those with limited financial resources.
criteria.whyItMatters: Sustainable products are affordable for all market sectors.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when pricing or access barriers are relevant to project outcomes.

criteria.summary: Maintains affordability for all market sectors.

criteria.label: Fair Trade
criteria.description: The project involves "fair trade" to ensure equity between low, middle and high income countries.
criteria.whyItMatters: Collaborations between low, middle and high income countries.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when labour, sourcing, or geographic equity are central to the project.

criteria.summary: Ensures collaborations between low, middle and high income countries.

criteria.label: Social Gaps
criteria.description: The project aims to close gaps of gender, power, or wealth within and across social, economic, and political systems.
criteria.whyItMatters: Reduces wealth and power gaps inside and between countries.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is most relevant when equity outcomes are explicit goals of the project.

criteria.summary: Reduces gaps in gender, power, and wealth.

criteria.label: Freedom of Expression
criteria.description: The project encourages or educates about democracy and/or freedom of expression.
criteria.whyItMatters: Encourages freedom of expression and/or democracy.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is most relevant when civic participation or expression is central to the project.

criteria.summary: Encourages freedom of expression and/or democracy.

criteria.label: Design Education
criteria.description: The project includes design students and/or enriches existing design school curriculum.
criteria.whyItMatters: Provides design education opportunities for students.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when educational engagement is part of the project.

criteria.summary: Provides design education opportunities for students.

criteria.label: Educational Component
criteria.description: The product includes an educational component that promotes sustainability to the consumer.
criteria.whyItMatters: Educates the user or consumer on sustainability.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion can apply across many project types.

criteria.summary: Educates the user or consumer on sustainability.

criteria.label: Endangered Languages
criteria.description: The project helps to preserve endangered languages, particularly Indigenous languages.
criteria.whyItMatters: Contributes to the preservation of endangered languages.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is most relevant when language preservation is part of the brief or audience context.

criteria.summary: Contributes to the protection of endangered languages.

criteria.label: Indigenous Culture
criteria.description: The project preserves or nurtures Indigenous culture other than language.
criteria.whyItMatters: Preserves or nurtures Indigenous culture.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is most relevant when Indigenous cultural contexts are involved.

criteria.summary: Preserves or nurtures Indigenous culture.

criteria.label: Local Culture
criteria.description: The project adapts to local and regional cultures.
criteria.whyItMatters: Adapts design to local cultures.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to most audience-centered communication projects.

criteria.summary: Adapts design to local cultures.

criteria.label: Cultural Diversity
criteria.description: The project promotes or enhances cultural diversity.
criteria.whyItMatters: Design promotes or enhances cultural diversity.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion can apply across many project types.

criteria.summary: Promotes or enhances cultural diversity.

criteria.label: Cultural Policy
criteria.description: The design entity and the majority of suppliers have a publicly-accessible policy to actively protect and support communities.
criteria.whyItMatters: Publicly-accessible cultural sustainability policy.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant but may be documented at the organizational level.

criteria.summary: Displays a publicly-accessible cultural policy.

criteria.label: Audience Engagement
criteria.description: The project engages end users throughout the design process or audiences that will be directly impacted by the project.
criteria.whyItMatters: Design process engages with end user.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant across communication design practice.

criteria.summary: Engages with end users and audiences.

criteria.label: Community Participation
criteria.description: The design entity actively supports and participates in the sustainable development of their community.
criteria.whyItMatters: Actively supports the sustainable development of your community.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant at the organizational and project levels.

criteria.summary: Supports the sustainable development of the design entity's community.

criteria.label: Practitioners' Education
criteria.description: The project results in the education of sustainability for design practitioners.
criteria.whyItMatters: Project educates others to support sustainable design education.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when professional learning or sector influence is part of the outcome.

criteria.summary: Educates design practitioners.

criteria.label: Economic Benefits
criteria.description: The project identifies and creates economic benefits beyond benefits to the client and the design entity.
criteria.whyItMatters: Adds value to benefit a region’s economy.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion can apply across many project types.

criteria.summary: Adds value that benefits a region's economy.

criteria.label: Profitability
criteria.description: The project budget or contract financially compensates the design entity.
criteria.whyItMatters: The designing entity profits from the project.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to most projects.

criteria.summary: Ensures the design entity is paid for work performed.

criteria.label: Unpaid Work
criteria.description: The design entity and the project did not request unpaid work, also known as "free pitching", "speculative work", or "spec work", from designers, including interns and student designers.
criteria.whyItMatters: All design work is financially compensated.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to all projects.

criteria.summary: Compensates all designers.

criteria.label: SMART Goals
criteria.description: A project document exists that establishes SMART financial objectives with clear, measurable targets and time-bound outcomes.
criteria.whyItMatters: Financial objectives are defined in a design brief.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to projects with defined financial goals.

criteria.summary: Outlines financial objectives in the design brief.
criteria.category: Economic Accountability and Strategic Value / Financial Planning

criteria.label: Accountability and Transparency
criteria.description: Adheres to transparent financial management and documentation practices.
criteria.whyItMatters: Adheres to international accounting standards.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion is broadly relevant to all projects.

criteria.summary: Adheres to transparent financial management and documentation practices.
criteria.category: Economic Accountability and Strategic Value / Financial Planning

criteria.label: Standards Improvement
criteria.description: The project improves the design entity's documented standards and procedures.
criteria.whyItMatters: Continuous improvement in the designing entity’s organization.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion applies when internal learning and process improvement are part of project value.

criteria.summary: Improves the standards and procedures of the design entity.
criteria.category: Economic Accountability and Strategic Value / Financial Planning

criteria.label: Design Thinking
criteria.description: Design thinking adds economic value to audiences, users, and/or stakeholders.
criteria.whyItMatters: Adds value to a business through design strategy.

applicability.notApplicableMessage: This criterion can apply across many project types.

criteria.summary: Adds business value through design strategy.
criteria.category: Economic Accountability and Strategic Value / Financial Planning

projectCategories.label: Print-based
projectCategories.description: Projects primarily delivered as physical printed matter.

projectCategories.label: Digital
projectCategories.description: Projects primarily delivered through screens, devices, networks, or electronic files.

projectCategories.label: Hybrid
projectCategories.description: Projects combining physical and digital components.

projectTypes.label: App
projectTypes.description: A software application or interactive digital tool.

projectTypes.label: PDF Report
projectTypes.description: A downloadable electronic document or report.

projectTypes.label: Packaging
projectTypes.description: Packaging for a product or service.

projectTypes.label: Exhibit
projectTypes.description: An exhibit or installation with physical and/or digital components.

projectTypes.label: Campaign
projectTypes.description: A campaign spanning multiple media touchpoints.

projectTypes.label: Social Media Asset
projectTypes.description: A social media post, story, or campaign asset.
